zh: 把合并过程画成一棵二叉树，每个初始值对总代价的贡献是它的值乘以它所在叶子的深度，所以越小的值应该被合并越多次。
这就是哈夫曼编码的结构：存在一种最优方案先合并当前最小的两个数，合并后问题规模减一、形式不变，于是每次都合并最小的两个即可。
把所有数放进最小堆。只要堆里多于一个数，就弹出两个最小值，把它们的和累加进答案，再把和放回堆。答案可能超过 32 位，用 64 位整数；值为 0 的元素同样适用。
en: Draw the merging process as a binary tree: each initial value contributes its value times the depth of its leaf to the total cost, so smaller values should take part in more merges.

This is the Huffman coding structure: some optimal plan merges the two smallest numbers first, and after that merge the problem keeps the same form with one fewer element, so always merging the two smallest works.

Put all numbers in a min-heap. While it holds more than one number, pop the two smallest, add their sum to the answer, and push the sum back. The answer can exceed 32 bits, so use a 64-bit integer; zero values work the same way.

explanationEn:
## Approach

With a min-heap, repeatedly pop the two smallest numbers, merge them, add the merged value to the total, and push it back into the heap.

## Proof of correctness

View the merging process as a binary tree: each initial value's total cost is its value times its leaf depth. The deepest sibling leaves can be swapped for the two smallest weights without increasing the total cost; contracting them gives a problem of the same kind with one fewer element. So some optimal solution merges the two smallest items first, and by induction the greedy is optimal; zero weights also satisfy the exchange inequality.

## Complexity

O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
